title: Agenda and scheduling
intro: How Case Files get onto a board meeting: site boards and their weekly slots, the ready mark, the cut-off and late cases, triage lists and chasing. Today the owner marks ready and the coordinator builds each session by hand.

questions.question: How should the hospital's boards be set up (one general board, or separate site boards such as Breast or Head and Neck)?

options.label: Admin list, site defaults (Recommended)
options.description: The root admin ticks boards from a default list (General, Head and Neck, Breast, Gynaecology, Thoracic, GI, Uro, Paediatric, CUP) and can add or rename.

options.label: One general board only
options.description: Every Case File goes to the same board; simplest; site boards can be switched on later.

options.label: Fixed list, no edits
options.description: The same site boards in every hospital; no set-up, but a hospital cannot match its own boards.

questions.why: T13 kept, G34, I21. Today a session is only a date and a title. Research: 28.5% of Indian hospitals with a board run several site boards (head and neck, gynaecology, breast, uro-oncology most often); Tata Memorial works in 11 Disease Management Groups.

questions.question: How should a Case File reach the right board?

options.label: From the cancer, changeable (Recommended)
options.description: The cancer picked at creation chooses the board (breast to Breast, CUP to CUP or General); the treating doctor can move it.

options.label: Treating doctor picks
options.description: No default; the doctor chooses the board each time, one more choice when marking ready.

options.label: Coordinator places it
options.description: The doctor only marks ready; the coordinator decides which board takes it.

questions.why: T13 ('Case Files of that group are its candidates'), I21. The cancer picker groups (T07, R05) already follow organ systems, so the board can come from them.
questions.skip_if: Skip if R10-Q01 answered 'One general board only'.

questions.question: Should each board have a fixed weekly slot (day, time, room) that creates its meetings by itself?

options.label: Fixed slot, auto meetings (Recommended)
options.description: Set once; Vaidyx keeps the next few meetings ready; the coordinator can cancel or move a single one.

options.label: Fixed slot, coordinator confirms
options.description: The slot suggests the next date; a meeting exists only after the coordinator creates it.

options.label: No slots, by hand (today)
options.description: The coordinator creates every meeting with a date and a title, as today.

questions.why: B16 today: New board session needs a date and title each time. Research: 47.4% of Indian boards meet weekly (ICMR-NCDIR); Victoria framework: at least fortnightly; NAVIFY and Philips keep a meeting calendar.

questions.question: When a Case File is marked ready, which meeting should it go to?

options.label: Next open meeting (Recommended)
options.description: It joins its board's next meeting whose cut-off has not passed; the doctor can pick a later one.

options.label: Doctor picks the date
options.description: The doctor chooses from the board's coming meetings each time.

options.label: Coordinator decides
options.description: Ready Case Files wait in a pool; the coordinator puts each into a meeting.

questions.why: Today the board date is typed on the Case File at creation (B2) and a session takes the Case Files listed for its date. With fixed slots the date can follow the board instead.
questions.skip_if: Skip if R10-Q03 answered 'No slots, by hand (today)'.

questions.question: Who may mark a Case File ready for the board?

options.label: Doctor; resident proposes (Recommended)
options.description: A resident taps 'propose ready'; the treating doctor confirms with one tap; both names are kept.

options.label: Treating doctor only
options.description: Residents cannot touch the ready mark.

options.label: Doctor or resident
options.description: Either marks it; the audit shows who did.

questions.why: B14: today only the owning department marks ready (mark_ready, owner action) and the coordinator is told. Settled: residents work under the treating doctor and cannot sign; I03 liked. The ready mark is not a signature, so the owner decides.
questions.notes: Dropped in validation (17 Oct): same as R03-Q04 (the resident sign-off rule includes 'mark ready').

questions.question: Besides the Pre-Authorization rule set in R07-Q05, what else must be done before a Case File can be marked ready?

options.label: A question for the board (Recommended)
options.description: One or two lines saying what the board should decide; shown on the agenda and the room screen.

options.label: Question and reviewed summary
options.description: Also a current Case File summary that a doctor marked reviewed; strictest, slowest.

options.label: Nothing more
options.description: The question for the board stays optional; only the R07-Q05 rule applies.

questions.why: Code: mark_ready needs only a protocol and a board date, not the check or the summary. I07 (question for the board before listing); I01 presenter mode shows the board question; NCG VTB template ends with 'questions for the tumour board'; research: missing information is the top cause of deferral (UK lung MDTs: 24% deferred).

questions.question: How should a meeting's agenda be filled?

options.label: Fills from ready marks (Recommended)
options.description: Each Case File marked ready joins its meeting by itself; the coordinator reviews and can remove one; unready ones are never ticked.

options.label: Coordinator ticks ready ones
options.description: Ready Case Files are offered; none joins until the coordinator ticks it.

options.label: All listed ticked (today)
options.description: When nobody marked any ready, every listed Case File is ticked (gap G22).

questions.why: G22: unready Case Files get ticked when no owner marked any ready. B16, J3. The coordinator does the chair's job (T19 note).

questions.question: May the coordinator add a Case File that its owner has not marked ready?

options.label: Yes, with a reason (Recommended)
options.description: Allowed; the reason is typed, the owner is told, and the minutes say 'not marked ready by the owner' (as today).

options.label: Only after the owner agrees
options.description: The owner gets a request to mark ready; nothing is added until they do.

options.label: No, never
options.description: Only Case Files the owner marked ready can be on the agenda.

questions.why: Today the coordinator can add an unmarked Case File and it is minuted as such (owner_ready on the agenda item). Settled: Case Files belong to their treating doctor.

questions.question: When should the agenda close to new Case Files (the cut-off)?

options.label: 48 hours before (Recommended)
options.description: The agenda locks two days ahead and goes to members, so heads can prepare; later cases follow the late-addition rule.

options.label: 24 hours before
options.description: More time for late reports, less time for members to read.

options.label: Each board sets it
options.description: Each site board picks its own cut-off; 48 hours by default.

options.label: No cut-off (today)
options.description: Case Files can join until the meeting starts.

questions.why: I06 liked, G23. Victoria framework: agenda out 48 h before the meeting. Bart's: radiologists spend about an hour preparing a board list.

questions.question: Who may add a Case File after the cut-off?

options.label: Coordinator, with a reason (Recommended)
options.description: The doctor asks; the coordinator approves with a reason; it shows as 'late addition' on the agenda and in the minutes.

options.label: Coordinator, Radiology and Pathology
options.description: Victoria rule: the radiologist and pathologist must also agree, since they prepare the case; slower.

options.label: Urgent cases only
options.description: Only a Case File the doctor marks urgent can join late; others wait for the next meeting.

options.label: Nobody: next meeting
options.description: After the cut-off every new Case File goes to the next meeting.

questions.why: I06, G23. Victoria framework: late additions need chair, pathologist and radiologist agreement. Settled: the MDT Coordinator does the chair's job (T19 note), so 'chair' reads as coordinator here.

questions.question: Who puts each Case File in a triage list (for discussion, for noting, not ready)?

options.label: Doctor at mark-ready (Recommended)
options.description: The doctor picks 'for discussion' or 'for noting'; 'not ready' comes from the check; the coordinator can change it with a reason.

options.label: Coordinator at cut-off
options.description: The coordinator sorts every ready Case File after the cut-off.

options.label: Doctor only, fixed
options.description: The coordinator cannot change the doctor's choice.

questions.why: I05 liked, G24. NHS 2020 Streamlining MDTs: each case is either 'standard of care, not for discussion' or 'for discussion'; Greater Manchester adds 'not ready'. Scope: clinicians choose the list; the AI only shows completeness and never labels a case 'standard of care'.

questions.question: Should Vaidyx send the readiness reminders by itself before the cut-off?

options.label: Automatic, coordinator can stop (Recommended)
options.description: Three days and one day before the cut-off, each owner with open gaps gets one grouped reminder; the coordinator sees what went and can switch it off.

options.label: Coordinator approves daily
options.description: Vaidyx prepares the day's reminders; the coordinator sends them with one tap.

options.label: By hand only (today)
options.description: Nothing goes out unless the coordinator presses Remind.

questions.why: B15: readiness and chase list exist, Remind and Remind owner are manual. K09: overdue never notifies; U17: 536 unread notifications, so reminders must be grouped. R14 sets the channels; R08 sets request due dates and reminders to departments.

questions.question: What should happen to a Case File that is deferred or not reached in a meeting?

options.label: Not reached moves; deferred waits (Recommended)
options.description: A case not reached goes first on the next meeting; a deferred case goes back to the owner until marked ready again.

options.label: Both to next meeting
options.description: Both move to the board's next meeting by themselves, marked 'carried over'.

options.label: Both back to the owner
options.description: Both leave the agenda; the doctor marks ready again.

options.label: Coordinator decides each
options.description: Nothing moves until the coordinator places it.

questions.why: Outcome types exist (decision, deferred, referred, not discussed: OCT12 feature 5); R13 settles them. Research: UK lung MDTs deferred 24% of cases, mostly awaiting results, so a deferred case usually needs something new first.

questions.question: Should board members get a calendar invite for the meetings?

options.label: Recurring invite per board (Recommended)
options.description: One repeating invite when the weekly slot is set (a calendar file that works in Google, Outlook and phone calendars); changes go out as updates; no patient names.

options.label: One invite per meeting
options.description: A new invite for every meeting with date, time, room and join link.

options.label: No invites
options.description: Members rely on Vaidyx notifications only.

questions.why: Nothing in Vaidyx sends calendar invites today. Products: NAVIFY and Philips keep a meeting calendar. An invite travels by email (R14 sets channels); patient details stay out of it (R15).
